protocol_type: Layered serial frame protocol (INCITS T11 Fibre Channel FC-2). The FC-4 ULP (e.g. FCP) hands an operation to FC-2, which frames it: each frame is SOF | 24-byte header | payload (<=2112 B) | 32-bit CRC | EOF, tagged with SEQ_ID/SEQ_CNT and the exchange OX_ID/RX_ID. Frames form sequences and sequences form exchanges. FC-1 encodes the frame (8b/10b or 64b/66b) with ordered sets; FC-0 serializes it at 1-128 GFC. Flow control is credit-based (BB_Credit + EE_Credit).

channels.name: Transmit serial lane (TX)
channels.description: FC-0 transmit lane carrying encoded frames and ordered sets at the negotiated GFC rate (8b/10b <=8 GFC, 64b/66b >=16 GFC); 128GFC aggregates 4 lanes.

channels.name: Receive serial lane (RX)
channels.description: FC-0 receive lane recovering encoded frames and ordered sets; embedded-clock with CDR.

channels.name: Ordered sets (FC-1)
channels.description: 4-byte K28.5-based transmission words: frame delimiters (SOF/EOF), primitive signals (IDLE, R_RDY), primitive sequences (NOS/OLS/LR/LRR).

layer_stack.purpose: Map an upper-level protocol onto Fibre Channel; FCP carries SCSI (FCP_CMND/XFER_RDY/DATA/RSP), also FC-NVMe / IP / FICON.
Services across a node's ports: striping, hunt groups, multicast.
Frame / sequence / exchange constructs, flow control (BB_Credit/EE_Credit), classes of service, login.
8b/10b or 64b/66b encoding, ordered sets, running disparity, word synchronization.
Media, transmitters/receivers, connectors, gigabaud signaling rates (1-128 GFC).

frame_format.structure: SOF | Frame Header (24 bytes) | Optional Headers | Data Field (0..2112 bytes) | CRC (4 bytes) | EOF
frame_format.sof_eof: SOF and EOF are FC-1 ordered sets; SOF variants by class (SOFi1/SOFn1/SOFi2/SOFn2/SOFi3/SOFn3/SOFf), EOF variants (EOFn/EOFt/EOFa).

frame_header_fields.description: Routing Control — frame category (FC-4 device data, link control, extended/basic link service) and information category.
Destination address identifier (24-bit FC address of the destination port).
Source address identifier (24-bit FC address of the source port).
FC-4 upper-level-protocol type (0x08 = FCP, 0x05 = IP over FC, 0x20 = FC-CT).
Frame Control — first/last sequence, exchange originator/responder context, sequence initiative, relative offset present, end-of-sequence, abort condition.
Sequence Identifier — identifies the sequence this frame belongs to.
Data Field Control — which optional headers are present.
Sequence Count — sequential index of the frame within its sequence.
Originator Exchange Identifier — assigned by the exchange originator.
Responder Exchange Identifier — assigned by the responder.
Relative offset of the payload, or a link-control parameter, depending on frame type.

sequence_exchange.frame: Smallest indivisible unit (header + payload + CRC), tagged with SEQ_ID and SEQ_CNT.
sequence_exchange.sequence: One or more related frames in the same direction with the same SEQ_ID, ordered by SEQ_CNT; the unit of error recovery.
sequence_exchange.exchange: One or more nonconcurrent sequences for a single ULP operation, identified by the OX_ID/RX_ID pair (originator allocates OX_ID, responder allocates RX_ID).
sequence_exchange.sequence_initiative: Passed via F_CTL; governs which side may transmit the next sequence in the exchange.

structure.Area_ID: bits 15..8 — group of ports within a domain
structure.Port_ID: bits 7..0 — individual port within an area

classes_of_service.description: Dedicated connection between two N_Ports with confirmed (acknowledged) delivery; full path bandwidth reserved for the duration.
Connectionless, frame-switched, acknowledged delivery; each frame is ACKed and uses end-to-end credit; frames may take different routes.
Connectionless, frame-switched, unacknowledged ('datagram') delivery; no ACK, only buffer-to-buffer credit; the common class for SCSI/FCP.
Inter-switch (E_Port to E_Port) control traffic for fabric routing and management; connectionless, acknowledged.

flow_control.buffer_to_buffer_credit: BB_Credit — managed link-by-link; the receiver advertises buffers at login and returns an R_RDY primitive for each freed buffer; essential over long-distance links.
flow_control.end_to_end_credit: EE_Credit — managed N_Port-to-N_Port for the acknowledged classes (1 and 2); the destination returns an ACK frame to replenish credit. Class 3 has no EE_Credit and no ACK.

login_protocol.name: Fabric Login
login_protocol.description: N_Port logs in to the fabric (F_Port at 0xFFFFFE); the fabric assigns the 24-bit FC address and exchanges service parameters (BB_Credit, classes, max frame size).

login_protocol.name: Port Login
login_protocol.description: N_Port logs in to another N_Port (or well-known service such as Name Server 0xFFFFFC) to exchange WWN/EE_Credit/classes/max payload and establish an end-to-end session.

login_protocol.name: Process Login
login_protocol.description: Establishes the FC-4 (ULP) session; for FCP it negotiates initiator/target roles and FCP service parameters.

information_units.description: SCSI CDB + LUN + task attributes (initiator -> target).
Target signals readiness for a data burst (target -> initiator).
SCSI data (one or more sequences, either direction).
SCSI status, sense data, residual counts (target -> initiator).

ordered_sets.note: Ordered sets are 4-byte transmission words beginning with the K28.5 special character.
